claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

claimant_dispute_unresolved.description: Whether two responsible claimants cannot agree who should claim Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 8 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old and lives with you.

Now I need to ask: **Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. A few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Are you responsible for Alex's day-to-day care - meaning you provide for his needs like food, clothes, and other essentials?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, that's actually a bit complicated. My ex and I both look after Alex - we're both responsible for him. We've been trying to figure out who should claim the Child Benefit, but we can't seem to agree on it. We're kind of stuck on that decision.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand - that can be a tricky situation. Let me clarify a few things to help you understand how this works:

According to the rules, only one person can get Child Benefit for a child. If you and your ex are both responsible for Alex, you should ideally agree between yourselves who will claim it. However, if you cannot agree, HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) will make the decision for you about who should receive it.

To help assess your situation better, can you tell me: **Does Alex live with you full-time, or does he split his time between you and your ex (for example, shared custody)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with me full-time. He's here at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex lives with you full-time and you're responsible for his care, that's an important factor.

Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is there anything else about your situation I should know? For example:**
- Is Alex in hospital or care?
- Does your ex currently claim Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else claimed it?
- Are there any other circumstances that might affect the claim?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nothing like that. Alex isn't in hospital or care or anything - he's just at home with me like any normal 8-year-old. And no, my ex isn't claiming Child Benefit for him - nobody else is getting it for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me summarize your situation and provide my assessment:

**Your situation:**
- You have one child, Alex, who is 8 years old
- Alex lives with you full-time in the UK
- You are responsible for his day-to-day care
- Alex is not in hospital or care
- Nobody else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

Based on the eligibility rules, you meet the key criteria for Child Benefit:
- You live in the UK
- Alex is under 16 years old
- You are responsible for Alex (you live with him and provide for his needs)
- Only one person can claim Child Benefit for a child, and nobody else is currently claiming for Alex

Even though you mentioned that you and your ex both have responsibility for Alex and haven't agreed on who should claim, the fact that Alex lives with you full-time is a significant factor. You would normally qualify for Child Benefit in this situation.

Let me make my final assessment now.
